title: Power Lens Laboratory
summary: One fictional institutional case and three analyses of power applied to the same five items, in the same order, every round. Each lens makes a different item the strongest evidence, leaves a different part of the file in shadow, and implies a different thing to go and change - and no single remedy reaches the other two mechanisms.
learningObjectives: Apply three accounts of power to one unchanged body of evidence and say what each brings into focus.
State what each account leaves in shadow, and why that is a cost rather than an oversight.
Recognise that some items are core to one lens and defensible under another, so the readings overlap rather than partition.
Explain why each lens implies a different intervention, and why no one intervention would have stopped the other mechanisms.
Distinguish applying a theoretical lens from establishing a fact about a case.
interactionTypes: constant case with a rotating analytic lens
single best-answer judgement per lens, from a fixed and unchanging option list
three-level key marking one strongest item, genuinely overlapping items, and items another lens owns
paired feedback naming what each lens foregrounds and backgrounds
withheld synthesis diagram of three parallel mechanisms and remedies
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. All processing happens in the browser and no responses persist after the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. Answered options are marked aria-disabled rather than disabled, so they stay in the tab order and can be re-read. Lens verdicts are signalled by border style and a glyph as well as by colour, and each carries a visually hidden sentence naming the state. The progress strip is an ordered list with aria-current. The synthesis diagram carries a title and a description stating the relationship it shows, and the same content appears as text in the three lens summaries above it. Programmatic scrolling honours prefers-reduced-motion. No timed content.
dataStatus: Fictional case. Brackwell College, its committee papers, its incident log and its staff are invented. No real institution, incident, inquiry or person is described, and no figures are presented.
simulationNotes: The key marking one item as the strongest evidence for each lens, others as genuinely relevant but not the sharpest exhibit, and the rest as belonging to another lens, is one defensible reading of an invented case, written to make the contrasts sharp. It is a teaching device, not a finding. The third lens names two harms - testimonial and hermeneutical - and item 4 is ranked the stronger evidence only because no other lens has any claim on it, while item 5 is shared with the second lens. A well-argued alternative ranking should be credited.
readmeTopic: power, critical analysis and the consequences of a theoretical lens for intervention
